He works across embedded firmware, custom PCB design, VLSI layout and software, including on-device machine learning on the ESP32-S3. He is open to full-time roles in embedded, firmware, hardware, VLSI or software engineering, and currently volunteers as an AI software developer at MatchingDonors.

## Featured project: EchoSafe

- [EchoSafe](https://github.com/Advk2k4/echosafe): an ear-worn wearable that tells deaf and hard-of-hearing people what a sound was and which way it came from. A group senior design capstone at UMass Amherst (Spring 2026); Aadvik was team lead and owned the ML pipeline end to end plus every software-hardware integration, and designed the directional alert system. Four MEMS microphones feed an ESP32-S3 that classifies horns, bells, sirens, gunshots and background noise on the device (91% accuracy), uses arrival-time differences between the mics to find the direction, and buzzes a haptic motor on that side. Five custom KiCad PCBs were designed; the capstone board was fabricated, brought up and stress-tested. The idea was checked with the hard-of-hearing community on r/hardofhearing (4,000+ views, about 30 comments). Aadvik is the only team member still developing it.

## Other projects

- [Farewise](https://advk2k4.github.io/farewise/): compares walking, cycling, transit, taxis and driving anywhere in the world with a time and estimated cost, plans multi-stop days and tracks travel spending. React, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, OpenStreetMap. Code: https://github.com/Advk2k4/farewise
- [MicroVibe](https://github.com/Advk2k4/microvibe): a predictive-maintenance fault lab built from a starter kit for Hackachusetts 2026 (solo). An ESP32-S3 streams 1 kHz vibration data; a Python dashboard learns a healthy baseline and flags brake drag and rotor imbalance with an FFT speed line.
- 3×3 mesh network-on-chip (VLSI coursework, Dec 2025): RTL through synthesis in Synopsys Design Compiler and place-and-route in Cadence Innovus, with mixed-level simulation to check deadlock-free routing.
- Custom VLSI accumulator (ECE 558, Nov 2025): transistor-level 1-bit and 4-bit ripple-carry accumulator layouts in 45 nm CMOS in Cadence Virtuoso, checked with DRC and LVS.
- [TinyTemp](https://github.com/Advk2k4/tiny-temp): a battery-powered thermometer on a custom KiCad PCB with an ATtiny85, TMP36 sensor and SSD1306 OLED.
- [Fooling a brain-computer interface](https://github.com/Advk2k4/foolingAI-547) (ECE 547, team lead, Spring 2026): changing two of 1,001 EEG samples pushed an FBCSP + SVM classifier to 21.6% misclassification while staying above the 20 dB imperceptibility threshold.
- [Digit recognition on an FPGA](https://github.com/epeter11/ECE332) (team project, Oct 2024): neural-network inference on a DE1-SoC with OpenCL and an ARM Cortex-A9.
- [Bias detection in automated hiring](https://github.com/Advk2k4/BiasDetectionModel): LLM-based fairness audits on 480 controlled résumés using the OpenAI API, TF-IDF and statistical tests.
- [SafeStride](https://github.com/sheldor1510/safestride): a campus walking-buddy web app; Best UX / Product Design Hack at HackHer413 (team).
- [UPlay!](https://github.com/sheldor1510/uplay): a location-based web platform; Best Beginner Hack at HackUMass X (team).
- [Real-time sign language recognition](https://github.com/Advk2k4/asl-app), [facial and text sentiment analyzer](https://github.com/Advk2k4/sentiment-analysis), [heart rate monitor](https://github.com/Advk2k4/heart-rate-monitor), [Medway](https://github.com/Advk2k4/medway) (clinic queue tracker, in progress), [FoodScout](https://github.com/Advk2k4/FoodRecs), and an interactive C-learning app (53 lessons across 11 units).
